convoLines.text: "I can't reach this properly. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"Every day it's angrier. I need it cleaned before it turns — I can't work a wound like this. Wrap it tight when you're done."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"We lost Rahul, Tone, Mateo and Guadalupe. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
It's quiet at the tree line. June doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then June grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 June is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Sleep's gone strange. I clean up other people's messes quietly at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
They speak. You understand none of it.
They answer at length. They nod back, slowly.
They answer at length. They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
They answer at length. You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. Sounds, and the shape of meaning just out of reach.
They glance toward their own thoughts; the exchange is winding down.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it, anyway?"
Zoe seems lighter — something good landed recently.
"Permit me: I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"You're wrong." Too fast. Zoe looks away. "Just... drop it, okay?"
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"We lost Rahul, Tone, Mateo and Guadalupe this week. I keep setting out extra portions. Stupid."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"I sleep with one ear uncovered, always. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Yeah? What's up? Don't look away from this."
"About grief — yeah, we never did get back to that."
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"Between us — Still on whether they can trust you."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Rahul owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
June nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I keep turning over the last thing Rahul said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"The fire feels smaller without Rahul. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"That's enough for now. It'll percolate."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
They answer at length. They nod back, a little quicker this time.
They answer at length. A smile, tired but real.
They answer at length. You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it. "Please?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
A gesture, patient and clear: palms up, then toward you.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
Miguel: "Don't just stand there — you've got opinions, right?"
Miguel seems lighter — something good landed recently.
"We're down to 6 liters of clean water. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"6 liters. That's today's drinking water, and then we're boiling creek water and hoping. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Beastmaster. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Go. But sit with what I said."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'Sleep's gone strange. I clean up other people's messes quietly at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning.'"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." June digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1533 kcal to the pantry.)
"The plan is the plan until it isn't. Then we make a new one."
"I do the small things right. The big things notice."
"Still on what's been happening."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Miguel nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing."
"God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid."
"A full night's sleep. Not safety, not answers — just eight hours where nothing needs me. That's my whole theology now."
"This matters — Still on what you're hoping for."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Don't look away from this."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Since Ziad died... I keep expecting to see Ziad at the fire. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
June nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I sleep in short shifts. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."

lines: d39: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Rahul Kulkarni is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d39: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d39: 🕯️ Rahul Kulkarni is dead — contest. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d39: What Rahul kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d39: "Rahul's gone." Mateo looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Rahul." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d39: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Thabo blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d39: 📖 LEARNED: Tireless Stride (Level 1). You walk like water downhill — no wasted steps, no wasted breath. Every mile costs 15% less.
d39: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.

d39: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).

d39: The warm hum behind your ribs is gone. The reactor went with Rahul's body — it does not come out, and it does not pass on. Hunger is back on the table. (One reactor per world, and the world already spent its one.)
d39: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d39: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Rahul Kulkarni, 39 days. The mantle passes to Thabo Maseko.
d39: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Thabo Maseko, 41 — a taxi driver. His hands know different work now: Green Whisper.
d39: The village's quarrel was with Rahul — and Rahul is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d39: At the grave, Mateo, Guadalupe, June and 6 more speak for Thabo — "Rahul trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d39: The fire knew Thabo before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.

d54: 📖 LEARNED: Debris Shelter (Level 1). A lean-to of branches and leaves beats nothing. Dead air is insulation.
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Star Navigation (Level 1). North Star is constant. Find the Big Dipper, follow the pointer stars. You always know north.
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d54: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Wire Snares (Level 1). A loop of wire on a game trail. Simple, effective, ancient. Check at dawn.
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 1). Ground them: 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch. Breathe with them. Slow is fast.
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Small Unit Tactics (Level 1). Flank, don't charge. High ground matters. Never split your group unless you have to.
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Improvised Weapons (Level 1). Everything is a weapon if you're desperate. A rock, a stick, a handful of dirt in the eyes.
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Managing Fear (Level 1). Fear is data, not orders. Acknowledge it, then decide anyway. Courage is fear that kept going.
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Tracking People (Level 1). People leave sign: broken twigs, footprints, disturbed earth. You can follow.
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Night Hunting (Level 1). Hunting at night is not hunting blind. It is hunting by ear, by smell, by patience.
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Shield Wall (Level 1). Shoulder to shoulder in the wilds, you brace as one. While an ally fights beside you, blows that reach you land softer — the line holds together or not at all.
d54: 📖 LEARNED: Tripwire (Level 1). You string a wire at ankle height. The next monster that moves eats dirt — prone, stunned, and embarrassed. (Sets up the party.)

lastSay: d62: ⚠ Haven's pantry is empty. Day 5 of hunger.
d62: Haven couldn't hold. On the fifth hungry day, people started walking — in different directions. The scattering, again.
d62: The garden is going weedy — your Muscadine Grapes needs tending, or the harvest halves.

d62: 💬 Pola pulls you aside. "I need to tell you something. Last night I... dreamed? No. I was AWAKE. And something spoke to me. Not the System — something else. It said: 'Tell the human to watch the nort
d62: (Pola has been contacted by an alien player. They don't understand what happened. But they'll warn you when they dream again.)
